ecu_aps.label: Throttle
ecu_aps.note: Range [0, 110] %: the pedal channel reads 104-106 % at full throttle on every development session (pedal / ECU calibration over-range, not a fault). A [0, 100] gate failed the channel on half the sessions and left every entry_1_brake phase empty; 110 covers the observed maximum (106.0) with margin.

log_dms_dam_fl.label: Damper Force FL
log_dms_dam_fl.note: Damper / pushrod strain-gauge force sensor (modules/loads.py). The range gate is a plausibility bound on pushrod force for this car (a few kN, generous both ways), not a sensor spec: it admits real dynamic excursions and fails a grossly corrupted channel (see log_dms_dam_fr).

log_dms_dam_fr.label: Damper Force FR
log_dms_dam_fr.note: Same channel family as log_dms_dam_fl. One development export carries a constant corrupted offset (about -15.95 million N), removed by channel_corrections.log_dms_dam_fr before this gate. Uncorrected, the gate fails the channel and the wheel loads fall back per corner instead of using the faulty value.

ecu_B_tc_act.label: TC Active
ecu_B_tc_act.note: Traction-control activity flag (clean boolean). Read by modules/setup_engine.py (tc_activity): a traction-limited exit ranks tc_lon above the differential. TC position channels exist in three agreeing domains (ecu_TC_int_pos / ecu_TC_tim_pos, log_tc_int_pos / log_tc_tim_pos, stw_rt03_tc_int / stw_rt01_tc_tim), but the LAT / LON mapping is undocumented and cannot be inferred (the values run nearly parallel), so no position channel is whitelisted and the TC setting stays 'current value not assessable'.

log_abs_pos.label: ABS Map Position (logged)
log_abs_pos.note: Trusted ABS switch-position channel: log_abs_pos / log_rt_abs_pos / stw_rt04_abs (dash / steering-wheel domain) agree, while the ECU-domain abs_switch_pos reads one step higher and is not trusted. Range [0, 11] = the rows of car_data.json's abs table (0 = off .. 11 = monsoon emergency). modules/setup_state.py reads the current ABS map from it, since the setup sheet has no ABS field.

log_susp_travel_fl.label: Suspension Travel FL
log_susp_travel_fl.note: Wheel / suspension travel (modules/loads.py), used to look up car_data.json motion_ratio_vs_wheel_travel. The range is a generous mechanical-travel bound (the digitised table spans roughly -80..+60 mm across both axles), not a precision spec.

corner_detection.brake_throttle_max_pct_derived_from: Tier B. The lift-off construction at 95 (last sample at or above it before turn-in = end of full throttle) was verified against brake pressure, derived on the development data (see thesis); the value 95 itself is set, not derived.
corner_detection.steering_unwind_fraction_derived_from: Tier B, no derivation: exit_4 ends where the post-apex steering has unwound to half its post-apex peak, the midpoint of the unwinding. Listed as a limitation.
corner_detection.lap_time_representative_factor_derived_f: derived on the development data (see thesis)

channel_corrections._comment: Decoding offsets for known-corrupt channels, applied in csv_parser before the quality / range gate, and only if the file's raw channel mean lies inside precondition_mean_range, so a healthy export stays untouched. Three offset classes: decoding faults (this block), event-specific logger zero entries (event_zero_entries, applied right after this block) and the static gauge-check calibration (wheel_loads.pushrod_offset_*_N, after the gate).

log_dms_dam_fr.derived_from: derived on the development data (see thesis)

event_zero_entries._comment: Event-specific logger zero entries. A gauge zeroed against a different reference at one event reads a constant offset there; csv_parser subtracts zero_N from the raw channel before the quality / range gate (otherwise the gate fails the channel and the wheel loads drop to the static split). An entry applies to a file only if (a) the header's TrackName and logger serial (and logger_software where given) match, and (b) the channel's raw mean minus zero_N lies inside that channel's own range gate in 'channels', so a gauge re-zeroed at a later event of the same track stays on the static split instead of taking a wrong entry. The NBR FR entry is referenced to the Paul Ricard FR offset including channel_corrections.log_dms_dam_fr; if that correction is re-derived, the FR entry must be re-derived with it. Accuracy: wheel loads from a corrected channel are 'L4 with an L2 zero' (logged sensor + motion-ratio table, zero entry an event measurement, per-corner u in the entries).
event_zero_entries._procedure: How an event gets its entry (documented, not automated): (1) check the event's files: header track / serial, raw damper level against the range gate; (2) preferred: the team's static zero check at the event, entered as a measured zero; otherwise per file and corner the gauge-vs-raw-voltage map offset minus the same car's Paul Ricard map offset, median over the event's files; (3) acceptance: u <= 700 N at the wheel and the load validation checks passing on all files of the event; (4) enter the medians with file spread and u. Limitation: the header carries no date, so two events of the same track and logger with near-identical zeros cannot be told apart.
